methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gallox Semiconductors is a Seed-stage chip design company founded by Jon McCandless and Debdeep Jena that has raised $5M+. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including 3 public comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Only one valuation method proved applicable: Stage-Progression analysis. Using the $5M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $12M. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow semiconductor peer set—while 11 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets yielded three or more datapoints necessary for robust median pricing, and a broad sector median would introduce unacceptable selection bias.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This single-method conclusion carries material uncertainty: the Stage-Progression approach relies on standardized multipliers that may not reflect Gallox's specific technology maturity, market conditions, or founder track record. The sparse peer set—0 same-stage semiconductors comparable—limits external validation. Key valuation drivers requiring deeper diligence include technical differentiation versus Etched and Tenstorrent, capital efficiency to Series A, and IP defensibility.
